text:
A: Hiya! Oh, it's you, I've been hoping I'd get you!
B: Well, that's the nicest welcome I've had all day! Martin. And you're Lisa?
A: Lisa, yeah. I saw the dog's tail in your picture and I thought, he's a dog person.
B: Biscuit. Labrador. Elderly and, er, generously proportioned. Vet says he's got to lose a stone. So have I, mind.
A: Oh, don't! Bramble's the same, she's a Staffy. She's on the sofa now, snoring. The vet looked at her and went, mm.
B: The vet's mm! I know that mm. Biscuit's got to go back for his ears next week. Costs more than my car, that dog.
A: Where are you, then?
B: Taunton, Somerset. You?
A: Ipswich. Suffolk. Flat, nothing exciting.
B: No, see, flat's interesting! I was a geography teacher. Flat land's where all the good drainage stories are. Somerset Levels, Fens, all that.
A: Ha, I'll take your word for it. My dad worked on the docks, he'd have loved you. You remind me of him a bit, actually.
B: Oh, that's kind. Is he still about?
A: No, he died five years ago. It's all right, though. You've got a look of him, that's all. The smile.
B: Well, I'm honoured. My dad was at a dairy, all his life. Sorry, love.
A: No, it's fine. Anyway! Have you got kids?
B: Two. Son in Bristol, daughter in Cardiff. Grown up and gone. House is proper quiet now, it's just me and Karen and the dog. She's a teaching assistant, still working, so it's just me rattling about most days.
A: Oh, I know that feeling. My Callum moved to Norwich two years ago. I still set his place sometimes at Sunday dinner without thinking. Dean takes the mick.
B: I still buy the cereal my daughter liked. She's twenty-six!
A: Ha! We're as bad as each other. Do you do anything to keep busy?
B: Pub quiz. I'm the geography and sport man. We lost by one point again.
A: Oh, I do a quiz! With my friends at the local. We're terrible, we just go for the chips.
B: That's the right attitude. And there's a folk night at our pub, I'll sing given half a chance. Loudly. Roughly in tune.
A: Go on, then, sing something!
B: Not in three minutes, I'd need a cider first.
A: Ha, fair enough. Karen's school doing anything for Christmas?
B: Nativity. She's in charge of the shepherds. Tea towels everywhere.
A: I do the tombola at our church fair! Every year. Same five of us.
B: Church Christmas fair, now that's proper. We go at Christmas, Easter, the odd Sunday when Karen gets me up. I always say I'll go more and then don't.
A: Me too. I say a little prayer when things go wrong, mostly.
B: That's most of us, I reckon, love. Most of us.
